_comment: Hook shapes from the 17 Sep 2026 audit of the highest-liked reels by live-assist AI interview brands (Final Round, Interview Sidekick, LockedIn, Parakeet, Verve) and Indian placement creators (PrepInsta, hiringhustle, freshersgpt, Mahima Hans). Every hook was read from the caption's first line; no video or audio could be played, so spoken and on-screen openers are not represented, and Instagram never exposes views, so the figures are likes. The brand mega-winners are concealment hooks: 'Interviewer has no clue he's using AI' (1.7M, reposted at least six times). On 17 Sep 2026 the owner lifted the brand rules: hooks and captions may say the interviewer did not notice, may call the overlay invisible or undetectable, may use the word cheating, and may tell fictional success stories ('she got the offer', 87.5K and 72.7K). Two things stay. The product line names supported screen sharing and every frame and caption carries the fictional-resume disclosure, which is what makes a story a dramatisation rather than a testimonial. And nothing states a guarantee, a statistic or a real customer, because there is no data behind one. Shapes below are the ones a validator-safe hook can take. promo_hooks are the on-screen headlines for the promo reel, 4-13 words, no banned words, no outcome; refresh them when a new audit shows different shapes winning. Correlation only: those reels won on their hooks, and a hook is not a guarantee.

shapes.name: When you are doing something ordinary and suddenly the interview is minutes away
shapes.example: Making roti. Interview in five minutes. Resume answers on your screen.

shapes.name: POV: the hard question lands and you are calm
shapes.example: POV: HR says tell me about yourself and your resume already answered.

shapes.name: A pain question with a twist in the second sentence
shapes.example: Answered everything, still rejected? You answered your question, not theirs.

shapes.name: One plain benefit, stated
shapes.example: Real-time answers from your own resume, in Hindi or English.

shapes.name: What the interviewer sees against what your screen shows
shapes.evidence: the softer cousin of the 1.7M concealment hook
shapes.example: Interviewer sees your face. Your screen shows the answer.

shapes.name: The interviewer did not notice; the answer was on your screen (the product line still says supported screen sharing)
shapes.example: Interviewer has no clue. Your screen has the answer.

shapes.name: Someone used it in a named round and it worked out, told as a fictional story under the illustrative disclosure
shapes.example: She kept the answer on her screen. Offer letter came Tuesday.

shapes.name: Never X again
shapes.example: Never go blank on why should we hire you again.

shapes.name: Is it cheating? asked, then answered
shapes.example: Is AI in an interview cheating? Her offer letter says no.

shapes.name: A named company and round
shapes.example: Infosys HR asks why Infosys. Your resume answers, live.

shapes.name: A small number of things to say
shapes.example: Three things for your TCS HR round, on your screen as you talk.
